indicators.note: the letters sit involved in, i.e. buried inside, the run of words cultural sociology

explanation.surface: Something else that plays a part in the study of culture and society.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are adverbs meaning in addition or as well.

clue.text: Software — so before this, use hand

parts.note: an app is a piece of software
in sol-fa the note that comes straight after so (soh) is la, so so comes before it
taken as written

explanation.surface: Instructions for a computer program: do this, then use your hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'so before this' is a riddle about the sol-fa scale: do, re, mi, fa, so, la... The note that so precedes is LA.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone a hand is to clap them, an idiom for an ovation.

parts.note: crumbs! is a mild exclamation of surprise; this is the version an old salt, a veteran sailor, would cry, and a shiver is also a splinter or crumb

explanation.surface: Bits of a stale seasoning, or of an aged mariner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crumbs' looks like a noun for fragments; it is the exclamation, and 'old salt' is a seasoned sailor, whose stock oath this is.
explanation.definitionFit: A pirate-style oath expressing surprise, used just as a landlubber says crumbs.

parts.note: the toast chin-chin is made from one word repeated, so its recipe is a doubled chin, and a fold of fat under the jaw has that name

explanation.surface: Asking whether a toast-making recipe calls for added fat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'toast' looks like grilled bread, but it is the drinking toast chin-chin, which is one word said twice.
explanation.definitionFit: A roll of excess flesh beneath the jaw is called by this two-word name.

indicators.note: after says the golf letter comes at the end, following the other piece

parts.note: if everyone loses there are 0 (zero, written O) winners: O + WIN
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A remarkable round of golf once all the rivals have been beaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outstanding' looks like praise for the golf but means unpaid. 'everyone loses' is read as zero wins: O WIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A debt that is outstanding is still unpaid, still due to be settled.

parts.note: boo is slang for a romantic partner or sweetheart
looking after number one means looking after oneself, i.e. me
called on the phone, i.e. rang

explanation.surface: A plea to return, as one's first-choice partner phoned.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb this word means to return or rebound, like the curved throwing stick.

clue.text: She comes out with me to turn over plant

indicators.note: turn over says the pair of pieces is flipped and read backwards

parts.note: a deb, a debutante, is a young woman who comes out into society
taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman emerges with the speaker to dig over a garden plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to turn over' reverses DEB + ME to give the answer. 'Comes out' is the social debut, not the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: To plant something is to fix it firmly in place, set it in surrounding material.

parts.note: he as in he-man, a word marking something male
a reward is a payment

indicators.note: into says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the take is the money taken in, the revenue
to hew is to cut, as with an axe

explanation.surface: A bandit's wages being slashed by the tax authorities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' gives THE WAKE. Hereward the Wake was an 11th-century English rebel who resisted the Normans from the Fens.
explanation.definitionFit: The Anglo-Saxon resistance leader was declared an outlaw by William the Conqueror.

indicators.note: hides says the first piece conceals the second within it

parts.note: nary is a dialect word meaning not one, never
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: An office worker who never conceals the accounts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'never' is the dialect NARY, as in nary a word, and 'hides' does the containing.
explanation.definitionFit: This legal official who witnesses documents is a kind of clerk, historically a scrivener.

clue.text: Is everyone splitting a last resort?

indicators.note: splitting says the second pieces go into the first and divide it

parts.note: per means a, as in five pounds a head
taken as written
all means everyone

explanation.surface: A question whether a full break-up is the only option left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' looks like an article but means each, as in so much a head; 'splitting' does the containing. The French phrase is used in English.
explanation.definitionFit: This French phrase names the worse option one accepts when nothing better remains.

clue.text: Grape for wine, particular thing I order

parts.note: a particular, fussy person is prim
it means a thing
taken as written
VO is the abbreviation for the Royal Victorian Order

explanation.surface: Choosing a grape variety for a wine, as a fussy customer placing an order.
explanation.definitionFit: This red variety of southern Italy, the same grape as Zinfandel, is used for wine.

indicators.note: parts means splits open, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: but means only, as in but a child
RN is the Royal Navy, one of the armed Services

explanation.surface: Only some components of a service rose in price.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parts' looks like a noun but is a verb: RN parts BUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that went up in flames was set alight and consumed by fire.

indicators.note: covering says the first piece wraps around the second

parts.note: a patch is an area, as in a patch of ground

explanation.surface: A repair patch put over a fresh bowl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bowl' looks like a dish, but a bowl is also a stadium; the question mark marks the example.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowl is a type of sports stadium, an enclosed venue with surrounding tiers.

clue.text: Prince of Wales dying to block dirty look

indicators.note: to block means to sit in the middle and obstruct, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a glower is an angry stare
end means death, dying

explanation.surface: A royal heir desperate to stop someone scowling at him.
explanation.walkthrough: Owain Glyndwr, anglicised as Glendower, was the last native Welshman to hold the title, and appears in Shakespeare's Henry IV.
explanation.definitionFit: The Welsh rebel leader proclaimed himself ruler of Wales in 1400.

clue.text: Break camp — result, fire put out

indicators.note: put out means disturbed, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Instructions for leaving a campsite: pack up, then extinguish the fire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' looks like dousing the fire, but it rearranges CAMP RESULT FIRE.
explanation.definitionFit: A bone fracture that does not pierce the skin is a clean break of this kind.

clue.text: Dutch province's butcher briefly seen in China

indicators.note: seen in says the shortened piece appears within the other

parts.note: china is rhyming slang for mate (china plate), a friend

indicators.note: briefly says the word is cut short, its last letter dropped

parts.note: to butcher is to slay

explanation.surface: A Dutch region's slaughterman makes a short appearance in China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' drops a last letter and 'seen in' does the containing. China plate is Cockney rhyming slang for mate.
explanation.definitionFit: This northern region of the Netherlands is one of its twelve provinces.

indicators.note: rough means disordered, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A ship has come into harbour while the sea is still choppy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rough' rearranges SEA STILL. 'Docked' looks like a ship in port; here it means having a cut-off tail.
explanation.definitionFit: A docked animal has had its tail cut short or removed.

clue.text: Will put up pressure in sexy strip club

indicators.note: put up in a down clue means written upwards, so read backwards

parts.note: Will Self is an English novelist, the first name standing for the surname

indicators.note: in says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: hot means sexy
P is the abbreviation for pressure in physics

explanation.surface: A writer raises the stakes in a racy venue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will' is the novelist Will Self; 'put up' reads his surname upwards in this down clue, and 'in' does the containing.
explanation.definitionFit: A place of sleazy sexual entertainment, such as a strip joint, is called this.

parts.note: a banger is something that goes bang, and racing uses one to begin each race

explanation.surface: Banger racing is a British motorsport of old cars crashing into each other; the clue runs into the next.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banger' looks like the old car of banger racing, but it is the device that goes bang at the start of a race.
explanation.definitionFit: A blank-firing gun signals runners or drivers to begin, so racing uses it.

clue.text: Old firm receives box containing a book

indicators.note: receives says the firm takes the rest inside it

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

indicators.note: containing says the box holds the single letter within it

parts.note: the box is slang for television, TV
taken as written

explanation.surface: An old company takes delivery of a box with a book inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'box' is slang for television; 'containing' and 'receives' nest the pieces one inside another.
explanation.definitionFit: A book of medium size, its sheets folded into eight leaves, is called by this name.

clue.text: … cars he may crash, avoiding shots

indicators.note: crash means smash up, so these letters are wrecked into a new order

explanation.surface: Continues the banger race: a driver who may wreck his car, dodging gunfire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crash' rearranges CARS HE MAY. 'Shots' looks like gunfire but means photographs.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone reluctant to be photographed keeps out of photographs, i.e. avoids shots.

indicators.note: not says the abbreviation is removed from the first word

parts.note: a rat, a despicable person, is a wretch

explanation.surface: A comparison of rodent and feline, as though the rat refuses to be in company with the cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cat' is British slang for being sick, as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To cat is slang for to vomit, and heaving or gagging is the same act.

clue.text: Hey Derek, make an off-peak call

parts.note: yo is an informal greeting like hey
Del is a short form of Derek, as with Del Boy in the sitcom Only Fools and Horses

explanation.surface: Telling Derek to phone during the cheap-rate hours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off-peak' looks like cheap-rate phoning but means sung off a mountain peak.
explanation.definitionFit: This warbling Alpine call is sung by a singer on a mountainside, so it comes off a peak.

indicators.note: using extra says one more letter is added into the first piece

parts.note: LEDs are light-emitting diodes, small lights
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: An urban area whose lighting consumes more power.
explanation.walkthrough: Leeds is a city in Yorkshire, northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a large city in West Yorkshire, England.

parts.note: an gives the indefinite article A
an office or department, abbreviated DEPT

explanation.surface: A specialist who works in an office.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a highly skilled, proficient person: plain synonyms.

clue.text: Supermarket make-up hiding spymaster's code device

parts.note: Aldi is a discount supermarket chain

indicators.note: hiding says the first piece conceals the second within it

parts.note: slap is British slang for cosmetics
M is the head of the secret service in the James Bond stories

explanation.surface: Cosmetics from a supermarket conceal a spy chief's signalling gadget.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hiding' puts M inside SLAP.
explanation.definitionFit: This signalling lamp flashes Morse code, used between ships at sea.

indicators.note: cryptic means obscure or encoded, so these letters are disguised in a new order

explanation.surface: Puzzle clues polished just as one would expect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cryptic' looks like describing the clues, but it rearranges CLUES HONED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something running to the timetable happens at the planned, expected time.

indicators.note: breaking says the second piece breaks into the first

parts.note: to clear a sum as profit is to net it
X stands for by, as in 3 by 4 = 3 x 4

explanation.surface: Winning by breaking free and getting clear.
explanation.definitionFit: Succeeding here means following on, coming after in order.
